rules.when: The task is a trivial change whose edit is already fully defined, such as a one-line fix, a config value change, or a rote rename.
rules.why: Trivial fixers: the change is already specified, so the cheapest fast model is enough. Luna leads; Sonnet stands in when Codex quota is tight, and Haiku 5.5 replaces Sonnet here once Anthropic ships it (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104749177456722354). Captain 2026-09-29: Luna paired with Sonnet.

rules.when: The task is planning a new feature, writing a spec, or investigating a complex or not yet understood bug.
rules.why: Planners: Kun's bucket 3 is Opus 5.5 almost exclusively, because only the frontier tier asks what the real goal is instead of how to get it done; Sonnet 5.5 is explicitly not an equal planner (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104749177456722354). GPT 6 Sol is now roughly Sonnet-equivalent (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104657437777408400), so it takes planning when Claude's window is exhausted rather than as an equal planner. xhigh because the work is not well defined yet.

rules.when: The task is an adversarial code review or audit of an existing change.
rules.why: Kun's bucket 4: Sol is the best adversarial code reviewer he has run, and he skips Astra here only because it is too expensive at review volume (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2103277022235766963). Opus 5.5 takes the review when Codex quota is unavailable.

rules.when: The task is highly ambiguous or creative work that truly needs premium intelligence, or an escalation to untangle a mess such as crewmates disagreeing, a spiraling review loop, or a simple change that grew into a giant PR.
rules.why: Premium intelligence and escalation untangling (Kun's bucket 2). Premium is expensive, so it runs only when the extra judgment is worth the cost; Opus 5.5 stands in when Fable quota is tight. Captain 2026-09-29: Astra runs alongside Opus and Sol here, and Sol covers the case where both premium accounts are tight.

why: Implementers (Kun's bucket 4): well-defined work goes to an efficient workhorse, not the frontier planner. Claude Sonnet 5.5 leads because it is fast, cheap, and smart enough to follow a plan (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104749177456722354); GPT 6 Sol is its equal in this tier (x.com/kunchenguid/status/2104657437777408400) and stays a first-class lane; Opus 5.5 spans almost every bucket and takes the lane when both are tight. Live quota picks whichever account has room.
